entry.title: Welcome to Lingual
entry.text: First things first a big thank you for downloading this app and being open to helping test this bad boy You won't be disappointed What exactly is this That's honestly a question that you'll have as much saying as I do But to keep it short this came from a question I asked myself a year ago namely what if computers didn't revolve around touching and looking at things to control them The computer is really just a tool But unlike physical tools like a hammer its function can be changed to perform different tasks But like a physical hammer it's user interface is fixed and prescriptive The levers you use to control the computer whether it be a desktop laptop or smart phone aren't really flexible to the end-user all the task at hand Today computers rely on your hands to communicate things via button presses gestures mouse clicks and they rely on your eyes to receive feedback on what it's executed In this way you're able to converse with your computer But what about when your eyes or hands aren't available Well I guess you missed out on all the super powers that computers unlock As much as people with motor or visual handicaps that are affected by this You are too There are broadly three classes of handicaps permanent temporary and situational Permanent handicaps are typically what we consider disabilities these include amputation or blindness Temporary handicaps are disabilities that occur over extended periods of time Something like breaking your arm would fall in this category The last class of handicaps are situational and these are moments where certain faculties aren't available to use When you're driving your eyes and hands are occupied so you technically can't use your phone Similarly when you're cooking your hands are too busy chopping carrots to do anything meaningful To add to all of this the pandemic has made it painfully apparent how reliance is become to touch and screens as a way of controlling our devices and this was revealed to us in a time where we were encouraged to distance from touch So what are the alternatives to touch input and visual output Voice input and audio output For ages speaking has been the primary way for humans to communicate with each other Language is a way of relating to others and sharing our own lived experience What if we tapped into this to communicate to our computers as well What's the voice Definitely more than just spoken content There are things like pitch speaking rate and loudness that we can tap into as a way to control our devices And when it comes to audio output it has long been the forgotten sibling to visual output but in many ways it can be just as powerful I'm a little content audio doesn't DeMond all your attention always This is why you can listen to music while working So why can't you browse the web while working to That's where lingual comes in The mission is to make computers more accessible using voice and audio as replacements or compliments to vision in touch so that anyone regardless of their ability or situation can use a computer effectively This requires leveling the playing field between using touch voice fission and audio which is what this prototype is exploring What exactly is this prototype That's cool it's a combination of a notetaking app and a voice note recorder The app allows you to create audio visual entries with just speech and hearing Spoken word is recognized and captured as audio and text that can be added deleted highlighted navigated copied copied copied pasted and stylized without needing to look or touch at the screen We don't use keyboards around these parts Meanwhile feedback is available both Aurilia spoken word or visually as text Speech recognition is at the heart and soul of those And yes I'm aware however Pramanick can be But think about it this way errors are only an issue if they're hard to correct If there is can be swiftly resolved much of the pain vanishes Why did I choose to make the snow That's a great question I'd say timing is great and the industry has the right ingredients to make this work AirPods of normalize the behavior of always on headphones It's no longer weird to be wearing your headphones when you're not using them And what this does is to remove the friction of having to pull out your headphones every time you want to operate an app that relies on them In addition the consumer-electronics industry is headed towards a world where does the contents no longer lives in the screen but now lives in the world That's what people call augmented reality and you're already seeing it today with face photos on social media What I'm building here is just a critical puzzle piece to enable that future and I'm pretty excited to have you help shape it Absurd quite a bit so I'll keep quiet now There's really no prescription for how you should use this app so feel free to explore and discover new use for it As you are using the tool though it would be great if you could note your experience using it also how you would imagine it evolving over time Lastly I challenge you to try to avoid using your hands or better yet turn away from the screen and see how effective you are using the prototype It takes some getting used to but once you do have a hang of it it's freezing and completely new Waze Please don't post anything on social media yet as we're figuring things out That said feel free to refer anyone you think would be interested in using or giving feedback This is a prototype so if you experience any issues don't hesitate to reach out And by the way this whole entry was composed using the app
